dialogue.content: こんにちは。お時間になったら始めさせて頂きます。よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Hello. We can begin now that it's our scheduled time. Thank you for being here.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you, likewise.

dialogue.content: ご相談有難うございます。まず初めに年齢と性別、相談したいことを教えて下さい。
dialogue.English: Thank you for reaching out. To begin, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you would like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 年齢45歳　女性　主人の事で相談したいです。
dialogue.English: I'm 45 years old, female, and I'd like to talk about my husband.

dialogue.content: ご主人の事ですね。どうなさいましたか？
dialogue.English: I see, it's about your husband. What seems to be going on?

dialogue.content: 主人の生活習慣だったり、自分の事ばかり優先で家族の事をもっと気にしてくれない事に最近イライラが止まりません。
dialogue.English: Lately, I can't stop feeling irritated by his lifestyle habits and how he always prioritizes himself and doesn't show more concern for our family.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。。。なにかきっかけの様な事はありましたか？
dialogue.English: I see... Was there any particular trigger?

dialogue.content: 娘の不登校がきっかけです。
dialogue.English: It started with my daughter's school refusal.

dialogue.content: もう少し詳しくお話できますか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me a little more about that?

dialogue.content: はい。不登校前までは喧嘩をしてもすぐに私から話かけて仲直りをしていました。
dialogue.English: Yes. Before she stopped going to school, even when we fought, I would be the one to initiate conversation soon after to make up.

dialogue.content: ええ。
dialogue.English: Mm-hmm.

dialogue.content: ただ娘が不登校になってからお互いの考え方にかなりの差を感じてきてしまいイライラが止まりません。
dialogue.English: But since our daughter stopped going to school, I've started to feel a significant difference in our ways of thinking, and I just can't stop being irritated.

dialogue.content: 考え方の差とはどんなところなのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: In what ways do your perspectives differ?

dialogue.content: 例えば、娘にかける教育のお金を私は親から沢山かけてもらったので娘がやりたい事は出来る限りしてあげたいと思います。
dialogue.English: For example, my parents invested a lot in my education, so I want to support my daughter as much as possible in what she wants to do.

dialogue.content: ただ主人は大学なんか行かなくてもあまり将来には関係ないといいます。
dialogue.English: However, my husband says that not going to college doesn't really affect one's future.

dialogue.content: それ以外にも休日をいつもテレビばかり見てダラダラと過ごしていてすぐに調子が悪いといいます。
dialogue.English: Besides that, on his days off, he always just lazes around watching TV and quickly complains about not feeling well.

dialogue.content: 相談者様が育った様に娘様にもしてあげたいのに、ご主人様は大学に行かなくても、あまり将来には関係ないと。それはご主人様は娘様に掛ける金銭的なことで仰ってるのですか？ご主人様の生活態度は歯がゆくなりますね。
dialogue.English: So you want to provide for your daughter the way you were raised, but your husband says that not going to college doesn't really matter for her future. Is he saying that because of the financial cost for your daughter? His lifestyle must be frustrating for you.

dialogue.content: わかりません。ただ私が主人に言ったのは「あなたは私立に高校からいれてもらい大学まで出させてもらっているのに大学に行かなくても将来はあまり関係ない」というのはおかしい。
dialogue.English: I don't know. But what I said to him was, 'It's ridiculous for you to say that not going to college doesn't matter much for the future when your parents sent you to a private high school and all the way through university.'

dialogue.content: 大学に行ってない人が言うならまだしも。。。説得力がないと言いました。
dialogue.English: If someone who hadn't gone to college said it, that would be one thing... I told him that coming from him, it lacks credibility.

dialogue.content: 確かに。ご主人様もしっかり親御さんから沢山掛けてもらったのに、ですね。大学に行く前の今の娘さんの不登校についてはなんと仰っていますか？
dialogue.English: I agree. Especially since your husband's parents spent a lot on his education as well. What does he say about your daughter's current school refusal, which is happening before college is even a consideration?

dialogue.content: 生活態度も娘の中の価値観に今の主人の生活をいれたくなくて。
dialogue.English: I also don't want his current lifestyle to influence our daughter's values.

dialogue.content: 好きな事をすれば良いと言います。
dialogue.English: He says she should just do what she likes.

dialogue.content: ご主人様の生活態度を娘様に見せたくない。そうですね。。。ダラダラすごして調子が悪いという大人の姿はあまり見せたく在りませんね。好きな事とは学校に行かなくても自分で好きな事好きな道を行けば良いという感じですか？
dialogue.English: You don't want your daughter to see your husband's lifestyle. I understand... One wouldn't want to show a child an adult who just lazes around and complains of being unwell. When he says 'do what she likes,' does he mean it's okay for her to follow her own path and interests, even if that doesn't involve school?

dialogue.content: はい。正直に話すと私も娘が不登校になる前まではダラダラと毎日を過ごしていました。ただ娘が苦しんでいる姿を見て一緒に頑張るしかないと今まで2年間頑張ってきました。
dialogue.English: Yes. To be honest, before my daughter stopped going to school, I also used to laze around every day. But seeing her struggling made me feel that I had no choice but to try harder alongside her, and I've been doing my best for these past two years.

dialogue.content: 主人が頑張ってないとは言わないですが、変わろうとしない所にイライラします。
dialogue.English: I'm not saying my husband isn't trying at all, but I get irritated that he won't try to change.

dialogue.content: それと好きな事とはそうです。学校じゃなくても構わないという意味です。
dialogue.English: And yes, by 'what she likes,' he means it’s okay even if it isn’t school.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね。頑張られた期間の2年間に驚きました。相談者様は変わる努力をされた。ご主人様にはその姿が見えないと。なのでイライラが止まらないのですね。
dialogue.English: I see. I'm struck by the fact that you've been working so hard for two years. You've made an effort to change. And you feel your husband isn't making that same effort. That's why you can't stop feeling irritated.

dialogue.content: はい。本人はしていると言います。ただ私からすると変わってる様に思えないんです。
dialogue.English: Yes. He says he is trying. But from my perspective, it doesn't seem like he has changed.

dialogue.content: 娘様の為に努力しているかというお話はお二人の間では良くするのですか？
dialogue.English: Do the two of you often talk about whether you’re making efforts for your daughter?

dialogue.content: はい。娘にはやると口にした事はやりなさい。と伝えています。
dialogue.English: Yes. We tell our daughter, 'If you say you’ll do something, follow through and do it.'

dialogue.content: ご主人様とはどうですか？
dialogue.English: And what about with your husband?

dialogue.content: してるつもりです。重複しますが娘に口に出した事はやりなさいと言ってるんだから私達がやらないのはおかしくなるからせめて娘の前ではしてほしいと。。。
dialogue.English: I try to. It's repetitive, but I tell him that since we tell our daughter she must do what she says, it looks bad if we don't do the same, so he should at least do it in front of her.

dialogue.content: 会話は出来ているけど、ご主人様はそれを態度で示していない状態なのですね。
dialogue.English: So you are able to have the conversation, but your husband isn't demonstrating it through his actions.

dialogue.content: はい。私はそう思ってしまいます。例えば禁煙すると言って電子だばこを吸っていたり。身体を気遣ってほしくて一緒にストレッチなどをする時もあるのですが一日中ダラダラとTVを見てる時もあるって感じですかね。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's how I feel. For example, he said he'd quit smoking but is now vaping. I want him to take care of his health, so sometimes we do stretches together, but there are also days where he just lazes around watching TV all day.

dialogue.content: 主人からは自分のペースがあるんだからいちいち指図するなといわれます。
dialogue.English: He tells me, 'I have my own pace, so stop bossing me around at every turn.'

dialogue.content: なるほど。禁煙はかなりハードルが高い宣言ですが、身体を気遣って・・・は相談者様がご主人様を思っての事なのでイライラしますよね。指図ですか・・・
dialogue.English: I understand. Quitting smoking is a challenging commitment, and your suggestions about caring for his health come from your concern for him, so it’s understandable you feel frustrated. 'Being bossed around,' I see...

dialogue.content: でも私からするともう2年も経ってますと言ってしまうんです。
dialogue.English: But I can't help but say to him, 'But it's already been two years.'

dialogue.content: どんな時相談者様はご主人様にその事を言いますか？
dialogue.English: When do you usually say that to your husband?

dialogue.content: 噛み合ってなくてすいません。
dialogue.English: I’m sorry if I’m not answering your question clearly.

dialogue.content: 大丈夫です、全然嚙み合ってると思っています。
dialogue.English: It's alright, I think you're making perfect sense.

dialogue.content: 主人が娘に継続する事が大事って言ったんです。でも主人はいつも自分が言った事をやる努力をし続けてるとは思えないと思った時です。
dialogue.English: It's when my husband tells our daughter that persistence is important. But I don't think he is continuously making an effort to do what he says he will.

dialogue.content: それは相談者様がイライラした時ということですか？
dialogue.English: Is that when you feel irritated?

dialogue.content: そうですね。
dialogue.English: That’s right.

dialogue.content: わかりました。確かに言いたくなりますもの。そこでお尋ねしたいのですが相談者様がイライラしていない普通の時ご主人様と会話する時間はありますか？
dialogue.English: I understand. It certainly makes you want to say something. On that note, I'd like to ask, do you have time to talk with your husband during normal times, when you're not feeling irritated?

dialogue.content: 毎日会話はしてます。
dialogue.English: We talk every day.

dialogue.content: では私からの提案ですが、普通の会話の中で相談者様のお気持ちを話してみては如何しょう。相談者様の気持ちを伝え、どうしてそう思うのかを伝え、どうして欲しいのかを冷静に話す。難しいですか？
dialogue.English: Then, may I make a suggestion? How about trying to talk about your feelings during one of those normal conversations? To calmly explain how you feel, why you feel that way, and what you would like him to do. Would that be difficult?

dialogue.content: いつも貴方はとか攻めるでは無く冷静に気持ちを伝える
dialogue.English: Instead of always attacking with 'You always...', calmly convey your feelings.

dialogue.content: それは何度もしてます。場所を変えて話をしたりもしてます。ただその時は自分が悪かったと言います。
dialogue.English: I've done that many times. We've even gone to different places to talk. But at the time, he just says he was wrong.

dialogue.content: 悪かったは何を悪かったと仰ってるのですか？
dialogue.English: What specifically does he say he was wrong about?

dialogue.content: 例えば、娘の学費を勝手に使って車を買われた時。主人の浮気を見つけた時生活習慣を話し合った時などです。
dialogue.English: For example, when he used our daughter's school funds to buy a car without telling me. When I discovered he was having an affair. When we discussed his lifestyle habits, and so on.

dialogue.content: それは悪かった以上の話です。私の方が冷静ではいられない内容です。。。。でも。だからこそ、普段は冷静にお話されている相談者は本当に家族全体をしっかり見ていらっしゃる事が伝わりました。
dialogue.English: That goes beyond just being 'wrong.' I don't think I could remain calm hearing that.... But. That's precisely why it's clear to me that you, who can speak about this so calmly, are truly looking out for your entire family.

dialogue.content: こんな話をしてますが私もかなりのクズ人間だったので主人の気持ちがわからなくもないんです。ただ親として娘が私達に変わるチャンスをくれたんじゃないかと今は思っているんです。不登校になってから娘の事を2人で良く話す様になり　だからこそ一緒に頑張ってほしいのに　。。。何か理由をつけて主人が逃げてる気がしてしまうんです。
dialogue.English: Even though I'm telling you all this, I used to be quite a mess myself, so it's not that I don't understand how my husband feels at all. But now I feel that as parents, our daughter has given us a chance to change. Since she stopped going to school, we've started talking about her a lot more, and that's exactly why I want us to try hard together... but I feel like my husband is just making excuses and running away from it.

dialogue.content: ご主人様はもしかしたら娘様の事を受け止められていないのかも知れませんね。２年も経っているのにと言う相談者様のお気持ちがイライラするのでしょうね。今日はご相談頂きありがとう御座いました。お時間が少なくなりました。相談者様のイライラ解決にお役に立てず申し訳ありません。懲りずにいつでもご相談下さい。
dialogue.English: Perhaps your husband hasn't been able to fully come to terms with your daughter's situation. And your feeling of 'It's already been two years' is likely what causes your irritation. Thank you for your consultation today. Our time is almost up. I apologize that I couldn't be of more help in resolving your frustration. Please don't hesitate to consult with me again anytime.

dialogue.content: 分かりました。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I understand. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: それでは今日はこれで終了させて頂いて宜しいですか？
dialogue.English: Then, shall we conclude our session for today?

dialogue.content: はい。大丈夫です。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's fine.

dialogue.content: 有難うございます。では終了させて頂きます。有難う御座いました。
dialogue.English: Thank you. We will end the session now. Thank you again.
